//: Module-prefix to architectural zone mapping used by layers.py.
Zone ids: 'internal-core', 'contrib', or 'product:<name>'.
Longest matching prefix wins, so a product's ddtrace.internal.<x>
subpackage can be carved out of the ddtrace.internal catch-all below.
Modules with no matching prefix are unclassified ('foundation') and
are exempt from every rule, both as importer and as imported module.
Direct children of the ddtrace package root that are deliberately left
unclassified (foundation code, exempt from every rule). layers.py's coverage
check fails on any top-level ddtrace/<x> package or module that is neither a
key in 'zones' nor listed here -- so adding a new top-level submodule forces
a conscious decision about which zone it belongs to, instead of silently
falling through with no rules applied at all.
A directed edge importer-zone -> imported-zone is a violation when:
- importer zone is 'internal-core' or 'contrib' and imported zone is any product, or
- importer and imported zones are two different products.
Same-zone edges, and edges into/out of unclassified (foundation) modules, are never flagged.
'exceptions' lists zone-pairs that are exempt from the above -- e.g. if we later decide a
product may import a security product directly, add {"from_zone": "product:x", "to_zone":
"product:appsec"} here rather than changing the detection logic. An exception may also carry
a "file_pattern" (glob, matched against the importing module's file path relative to the repo
root, e.g. "ddtrace/contrib/internal/*/patch.py") to scope it to specific files instead of the
whole zone pair -- use this for a one-off import that shouldn't set precedent for the rest of
the zone.

exceptions.//: contrib/* are tracer integrations; they attach to the Tracer/Pin/Span API by design
contrib/__init__ is the connection point for the event bus between llmobs and contrib
